alt: Poster: Tax and Compliance Corner. F&O losses are non-speculative business losses; same-year set-off against other heads but not salary; carry forward 8 years against business income if return filed by due date
text:
An F&O loss is not a capital loss. For tax, it is a business loss, and the rules for using it are specific.

Under the Income Tax Department's guidance, a non-speculative business loss can be set off in the same year against income under other heads, but not against salary. Any balance can be carried forward for 8 years and set off only against business income. Exchange-traded derivatives on a recognised exchange are excluded from the definition of a speculative transaction, so F&O losses fall in this non-speculative category. The treatment is unchanged under the Income-tax Act, 2025 (in force from 1 April 2026); only the section numbers differ.

The condition that is easy to miss: carry-forward rights depend on filing the return on or before the due date. A belated return ordinarily does not preserve the right to carry forward the loss. The loss also has to be disclosed in the return itself.

Our view: the filing date can matter as much as the trade when a loss is involved. That is an interpretation, not advice.
